## Pros

- Newborn mode built in and included ("Infant Nest Mode"), to 50 lb (maker); a CPST reviewer called it "so flat" (sponsored, not measured).
- One-hand auto-fold that stands on its own (manual; Babylist, Stroller Mom).
- Handled cobblestones, gravel and uneven streets well (Stroller Mom, sponsored; Babylist).
- Maker chart names the Aria V2 explicitly (November 2026); a strap adapter is included. Lifetime frame warranty.

## Cons

Misuse risks come first.

- **Misuse risk:** the FlexConnect strap is tightened by hand with no tension indicator; a loose, twisted or mis-routed strap gives no cue. The only check is pulling up on the carrier (FlexConnect manual).
- **Misuse risk:** the adapter has a wrong peg (the Nest Mode peg) right beside the right one, and setup needs full recline, leg rest up, brake on and harness fastened (manual).
- **Misuse risk:** straps left on the stroller are a strangulation hazard; remove them when not in use (manual).
- No reviewer has used an UPPAbaby seat on it; carrier stability and height unknown.
- New in autumn 2026; no measured weight, no gate-check or durability reports yet. Main hands-on review is sponsored.
- Does not fit the 22 x 14 x 9 in overhead bin on published size, despite the maker's "IATA-compliant" claim.
- Earlier Mockingbird Single and Single-to-Double lots were recalled in 2022-23 because the lower frame could crack (CPSC 23-042, 23-161). Current models are not named.
